thread.title: House passes Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act to restore veterans' firearm rights
thread.title_full: House passes Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act to restore veterans' firearm rights

author: Buckeye Reporter
title: House passes Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act to restore veterans' firearm rights
text:
The U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R.1041, the Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act, on May 21. The bill, sponsored by Chairman Mike Bost of Illinois, aims to reverse a policy that removed veterans’ rights to keep and bear arms without due process if they were assigned a fiduciary to manage their Department of Veterans Affairs benefits.
According to the bill’s supporters, it would allow veterans to receive benefits and assistance without fear of losing their ability to purchase and possess firearms. John Commerford, executive director of NRA-ILA, said, “This vote represents a significant victory and another step in the right direction of eradicating this terrible practice and should be celebrated by veterans and all Americans alike.” He continued, “On behalf of millions of NRA members and veterans nationwide, we applaud the U.S. House for voting to protect our veterans and honoring their service by ensuring that they are not treated as second-class citizens.”
NRA-ILA thanked Chairman Bost for his leadership on the issue as well as Speaker Mike Johnson, Majority Leader Steve Scalise, Majority Whip Tom Emmer, and other representatives who cosponsored the legislation. The organization also called on Senate Majority Leader John Thune and the U.S. Senate to pass the act so it can be signed into law.
Supporters argue that passing this legislation would close what they describe as a “shameful chapter” in VA history regarding firearm restrictions for disabled veterans with fiduciaries.
Buckeye Firearms Association advocates for individuals’ right to own firearms for legal pursuits such as self-defense, hunting, competition and recreation; delivers alerts on gun rights laws; offers updates on related legislation; provides training information; focuses its grassroots efforts in Ohio; and centers its activities within Ohio, according to the official website .
summary: The bill, sponsored by Chairman Mike Bost of Illinois, aims to reverse a policy that removed veterans’ rights to keep and bear arms without due process if they were assigned a fiduciary to manage their Department of Veterans Affairs benefits. According to the bill’s supporters, it would allow veterans to receive benefits and assistance without fear of losing their ability to purchase and possess firearms.
